title: Truthiness, falsy values, and guard patterns
hook: In an `if` statement, JavaScript does not ask 'is this true?' — it asks 'is this falsy?' Eight values are falsy; everything else is truthy. That includes empty arrays and `{}`.

blocks.text: **Truthy** and **falsy** describe how values behave in boolean contexts (`if`, `while`, `&&`, `||`, ternary `?`). JavaScript applies **ToBoolean** before branching. The **eight falsy values** are: `false`, `0`, `-0`, `0n`, `''` (empty string), `null`, `undefined`, and `NaN`. Everything else — including `'0'`, `'false'`, `[]`, and `{}` — is **truthy**. The **nullish coalescing operator (`??`)** returns the right side only for `null` or `undefined`, not for other falsy values.

entries.plainDefinition: A value that coerces to false in boolean context. Exactly eight exist in JavaScript.
entries.example: `if ('')` — empty string is falsy; body skipped.

entries.plainDefinition: Any value that is not falsy. `[]`, `{}`, and `'0'` are truthy.
entries.example: `if ('0')` — body runs because non-empty string is truthy.

entries.plainDefinition: Returns right operand only when left is `null` or `undefined`. Does not treat 0 or '' as missing.
Short-circuits to undefined when left side is nullish — no truthiness involved.

blocks.text: `if (userInput)` rejects `0` and `''` even when they are valid values. A retry counter of `0` is valid but `value || default` replaces it with `default`. Use `??` for nullish defaults and explicit comparisons for booleans. `document.getElementById` returns `null` (falsy) when missing — but an empty `<div>` is truthy. C# does not use truthiness — `if (count)` is a compile error unless `count` is `bool`.

blocks.title: Guard pattern picker
blocks.body: Missing value only → `??`. Any falsy → `||` (rare — know the 8 falsy values first). Explicit boolean → `=== true` or `Boolean(x)` when converting intentionally. Existence check → `x != null` or `x !== undefined` depending on intent.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: 0, -0, 0n
items.body: Zero in number, signed zero, and BigInt zero.

items.title: '' (empty string)
items.body: Empty string is falsy; `'0'` and `' '` (space) are truthy.

items.title: null and undefined
items.body: Missing object reference and uninitialized value.

items.title: NaN
items.body: Not-a-Number from failed parse — also falsy.

diagram.title: || vs ?? decision
diagram.source:
flowchart TD
  START["Need default value"] --> Q{"Is left side null or undefined?"}
  Q -->|"only care about nullish"| COAL["Use ??"]
  Q -->|"any falsy including 0 and ''"| OR["Use ||"]
  Q -->|"need explicit check"| EQ["Use === null or === undefined"]

snippet.label: Falsy vs truthy surprises
snippet.code:
const falsyValues = [false, 0, -0, 0n, '', null, undefined, NaN];
falsyValues.forEach(v => console.log(Boolean(v))); // all false

console.log(Boolean('0'));    // true — non-empty string
console.log(Boolean('false')); // true — string 'false' is truthy!
console.log(Boolean([]));     // true — empty array is truthy
console.log(Boolean({}));     // true — empty object is truthy
console.log(Boolean(document.all)); // false in modern browsers — legacy quirk
snippet.explanation: Lines 1–2: the canonical eight falsy values. Lines 4–7: common interview traps — string `'0'` and `'false'` are truthy. Line 8: `document.all` is a rare ninth falsy in browsers (historical).

snippet.label: || vs ?? in production
snippet.explanation: Lines 3–7: `||` treats 0 as missing; `??` preserves 0. Lines 13–15: `||` replaces empty string; `??` keeps it. Choose based on whether 0/'' are valid data.

snippet.label: Guard patterns for APIs
snippet.explanation: Line 3: `== null` catches both null and undefined. Line 8: explicit `=== true` when false is meaningful. Line 11: `||` intentional for empty name. Line 14: `??` for timeout where 0 might be valid.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Using `if (value)` when `0` or `''` are valid. Using `||` when you mean `??`. Assuming `[]` or `{}` are falsy. Checking `if (array)` to detect empty array — use `array.length === 0`. Confusing `??` with `||` when setting numeric defaults.

blocks.text: ToBoolean is the spec operation behind every boolean context. `&&` and `||` return the actual operand value, not a boolean — `0 || 'default'` returns `'default'`; `'hello' && 42` returns `42`. Short-circuit evaluation matters for `obj && obj.method()`. `??` cannot mix with `||`/`&&` without parentheses (syntax error) because of precedence ambiguity. `Boolean(0n)` is false. `document.all` is falsy in HTML5 for backwards compatibility. TypeScript `@typescript-eslint/strict-boolean-expressions` forces explicit comparisons in conditionals — best practice for large codebases.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Listing only six falsy values and forgetting `0n` or `NaN`. Saying `[]` is falsy. Not knowing difference between `||` and `??`. Using `if (x)` when x can be 0 in a counter or price field.

interviewTakeaways: Eight falsy values: false, 0, -0, 0n, '', null, undefined, NaN.
Empty arrays, empty objects, and string '0' are truthy.
Use ?? for nullish defaults; use || only when any falsy should trigger fallback.
&& and || return operands, not booleans — short-circuit evaluation.
60s: Eight falsy values. [] is truthy. ?? for null/undefined only. || for any falsy. Explicit === for booleans.
commonPitfalls: Weak: 'Falsy means empty or zero.' Strong: 'Exactly eight values; [] and {} are truthy.'
Using value || default when 0 is valid — use ?? instead.
Strong answer: '?? nullish only. || any falsy. if(x) dangerous for 0. Eight falsy values by spec.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: TypeScript ESLint flags `if (count)` when count is number — require `count !== 0` or explicit boolean. Prevents truthiness bugs at compile time.
C# requires `bool` in if/while — no implicit truthiness. `if (count)` does not compile. Null checks use `is null` or `== null`.
